🇮🇳 India is preparing to put corporate bonds onchain

India plans to launch its first tokenised corporate bond issuance in September, according to Reuters.

The pilot will involve state-owned power financier REC and bonds worth less than 5 billion rupees, approximately $57 million.

Blockchain will be used to record:

• issuance
• ownership
• trading
• settlement

Investors will purchase the bonds using India’s wholesale central bank digital currency. They will need both a CBDC wallet and a new digital securities wallet called DEMAT 2.0.

The pilot will initially be available only to selected investors. A secondary market is expected to follow in December.

The important point is that these bonds are not being turned into speculative crypto assets.

They remain regulated debt instruments. Blockchain changes the infrastructure behind them by allowing ownership and settlement to be recorded on the same digital system.

This is where tokenisation becomes practical.

The asset remains familiar.

The process behind it becomes faster and more programmable.

🔗 Source: Reuters⁠

🔻 THE TECHNICIAN WHO WATCHED THE AGE CLOCK RUN BACKWARD: CHAMBER 06 🔻

“At 02:17 AM, an 82-year-old man entered the chamber in a wheelchair.

Forty-eight minutes later, the biometric system identified the body in front of me as 38.”

⟁

For eleven years, I worked as a systems technician at ASTERION—a facility located 420 feet beneath an abandoned research station in northern New Mexico.

The surface had empty offices and broken satellite dishes. Underground were four operational levels, 186 personnel, and twelve medical chambers arranged around a circular control room.

My assignment was Chamber 06.

The official name on our screens was:

CRU-6 / CELLULAR REVERSION UNIT.

Before every procedure, the system searched for three things: the patient’s current biological condition, the oldest undamaged DNA pattern still stored inside the cells, and something the engineers called the “Original Body Memory.”

I once asked my supervisor what that meant.

He said: “The body remembers every version of itself. We only tell it which version to become.”

⟁

On October 11, 2023, they brought in Patient 0814.

Male. Eighty-two. Cardiac damage. Kidney failure. Severe joint degeneration. Unable to stand without assistance.

One line in his file was marked red:

AUTHORIZED FOR FULL REVERSION.

At 02:17 AM, the canopy closed. A low vibration filled the room. Thousands of blue-white points formed a perfect human outline around his body.

Then the screen changed:

CHRONOLOGICAL AGE: 82.4
BIOLOGICAL AGE: 79.1
TARGET TEMPLATE: 38.0
CELLULAR MEMORY LOCK: CONFIRMED

The number began falling.

76. 68. 57. 44.

At 03:05 AM, it stopped at 37.8.

⟁

When the canopy opened, the man sat up without help.

The spots on his hands were gone. His tremor had stopped. The surgical scar across his chest had faded to a thin pink line.

Then he stood.

Not slowly. Not carefully. He stood as if his body had never forgotten how.

He looked through the glass and asked:

“How long have you had this?”

Nobody answered.

“My wife died waiting for a heart transplant,” he said. “How long have you had this?”

Security entered thirty seconds later. The audio feed was cut. Patient 0814 was removed through a corridor my clearance could not access.

I never saw him again.

⟁

By morning, every record was gone. The procedure log said “routine electrical maintenance.” The footage had been replaced by a black screen.

But nineteen seconds of biometric data survived on my calibration terminal:

82.4 → 37.8

In eleven years, I witnessed 312 procedures. Only nine were authorized for Full Reversion.

Three weeks later, Chamber 06 was dismantled and moved to a location listed only as HAVEN NORTH.

Before the system went offline, one message appeared across every terminal:

PHASE II COMPLETE.
CIVILIAN READINESS: CONFIRMED.
PUBLIC ACCESS: DENIED.

CODE: ASTERION / CHAMBER-06 / BODY-MEMORY / FULL-REVERSION

They told you aging was a one-way road.

What if they already found the return route—and locked the gate behind them?

♟

Your body may not have forgotten youth. It may only be waiting for the correct instruction.
